question: How was it finally proved, in 1976, that four colours are enough for any map?
answer: By computer. Kenneth Appel and Wolfgang Haken reduced every possible map to 1,936 configurations, then had a computer check them one by one, more than anyone could verify by hand. Many mathematicians were uneasy. A simpler proof followed in 1996, and in 2005 one checked entirely by computer.
move: Trust in a result rests on how it can be checked, by hand or machine.
ask: Which result do I accept that I could never check, and why do I trust it?
source: Thomas, The four colour theorem, Georgia Institute of Technology
